reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that the proposal contains no redline (rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals) and no counterparty comment, so there is no risk of an invalid or directionally wrong edit.

The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 11.6 is a reciprocal, surviving (per Section 12.4) obligation to destroy Confidential Information on request and certify destruction in writing, with retention limited to archival/back-up copies — no unilateral or immediate deletion, so the walk-away scenario is not present.

Transition/exit machinery plainly exists (Section 12.3(c)(iv)–(vi) regulatory materials/data transfer and 'Transition Assistance'; Section 12.3(e) 'all reasonable assistance' from RevMed), and the deterministic check confirms data-return/transition language is present, so a 'missing clause' insert would be over-flagging.

The rationale correctly reads the commercial direction (as licensee, we are the party owing reversion/transition obligations, and we should not expand obligations binding us) and appropriately notes the shortfalls versus preferred wording (destruction rather than machine-readable return; 'promptly' rather than a fixed 30-day outside date) as rationale-level observations rather than deviations, per the playbook's classification semantics.
